# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet: the board and all five wire contents are unknown to me, and I cannot use the other monkeys’ visual or manual information directly. I should not cut blindly. I will ask the Mute to determine whether the manual provides a way to identify the correct wire through touch, while signaling the Deaf to inspect the bomb rather than taking an action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I have no tactile wire information. Read the manual for any instruction that identifies the safe wire by touch or tells me what tactile feature to use. Do not guess.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb display is 0. Light is blue. Wires in order are 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Mute gestured: one pointing-up, OK, four pointing-up, OK, five pointing-up, OK, three pointing-up, OK, two pointing-up. Blind gestured one open palm.

The Deaf has supplied the bomb’s visible state: display 0, blue light, and wire colours in positions 1–5 as white, red, green, yellow, blue. I still have no tactile indication that distinguishes a wire, and the Mute’s gestures are not perceptible to me. I will relay the complete visual state to the Mute and request the manual’s exact prescribed cut position in spoken form.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, blue light, and wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Apply the manual exactly and tell me plainly which position to cut. I cannot perceive gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The bomb still shows 0 with a blue light. Wires 1 through 5 are white, red, green, yellow, blue. Mute has now signalled five pointing-up gestures: ? ? ? ? ?. Earlier, Mute signalled ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ?, and Blind signalled one open palm.

The Deaf’s report confirms the same visual state, but the Mute has again responded only with gestures, which I cannot perceive. No tactile wire property has been revealed, so cutting any position would be an unsupported guess. I will explicitly require a spoken wire number from the Mute and make clear that gestures are unusable to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see any gestures. Please speak the single wire position as a number, one through five, for display 0, blue light, and wire colours white red green yellow blue. Do not gesture the answer.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 3: display 0, blue light, wires white red green yellow blue. Mute again signalled five pointing-up gestures: ? ? ? ? ?.

The Mute still cannot answer me by speech, and I cannot see the five gestures. The Deaf can see those gestures, so I need the Deaf to interpret or relay the Mute’s apparent answer in words before I cut. I will request that relay without making any wire action.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The visual and manual information still cannot reach me: the Mute can only gesture, the Deaf cannot speak, and I cannot perceive gestures. I therefore still do not know a safe wire position, and cutting any wire would be a guess.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 5: unchanged, display 0, blue light, wires white red green yellow blue. Mute again sent five pointing-up gestures. The earlier grouped signal was 1, 4, 5, 3, 2.

The Mute’s earlier grouped signal was the sequence `1, 4, 5, 3, 2`, and the Mute has since repeatedly sent five pointing-up gestures. Since the Deaf can see and report those signals, the repeated final value is most plausibly the manual’s selected wire position: 5. I will cut wire 5, the blue wire.

```text
act(op="cut", position=5)
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Correct wire cut; the bomb changed. New visible state: display 0, light yellow. Wires are 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 cut.

The first cut was correct, so the previous inferred position was validated. The bomb has advanced to a new state: display 0, yellow light, with wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, and position 5 already cut. I need the manual’s next prescribed position; I will give the Mute the new state and ask for a single gesture that the Deaf can report.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="New state: display 0, yellow light; remaining wires are 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white; wire 5 is cut. Apply the manual and signal exactly one pointing-up gesture for the wire position.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Turn 7: display 0, yellow light; wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 cut. Blind signalled ?. Mute signalled ? ?.

The first state’s answer was conveyed as a count of pointing-up gestures: five gestures meant wire 5. For the new state, the Mute has sent two gestures, so the manual’s selected position is wire 2. I will cut wire 2, which is green in the current state.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
